title: Prepositions of Place
summary: Describe location with em, no, na, perto de, longe de, dentro de, fora de, em cima de, and embaixo de.

sections.heading: Basic location with em
sections.body: Use **em** for location, usually contracted with articles: **no, na, nos, nas**. Portuguese often uses one preposition where English uses in, on, or at.

examples.en: The book is on the table.

examples.note: no article with many city names

sections.heading: Relative position
sections.body: Many place expressions use **de** after them. If an article follows, de contracts: **do, da, dos, das**.

examples.pt: O banco fica perto da praça.
examples.en: The bank is near the square.

examples.pt: Minha casa fica longe do centro.
examples.en: My house is far from downtown.

examples.pt: O cachorro está embaixo da cama.
examples.en: The dog is under the bed.

sections.heading: Inside, outside, in front, behind
sections.body: Use **dentro de**, **fora de**, **na frente de**, **atrás de**, and **ao lado de** for precise location. In Brazil, **em frente a** is also common for 'in front of'.

examples.pt: As chaves estão dentro da mochila.
examples.en: The keys are inside the backpack.

examples.pt: O ponto de ônibus fica em frente ao prédio.
examples.en: The bus stop is in front of the building.

examples.pt: A farmácia fica ao lado do mercado.
examples.en: The pharmacy is next to the market.

keyPoints: Em contracts with articles: no, na, nos, nas.
Many location phrases require de: perto de, longe de, dentro de.
De contracts with articles after place expressions.
Use ficar or estar for location depending on whether you mean situated or currently located.

commonMistakes.wrong: O livro está em a mesa.

commonMistakes.note: Use perto de + aqui = perto daqui.
